reason: Source + metadata are excellent, but every image on the museum's OWN infrastructure is destroyed by a dense, full-frame tiled 'Nederlands Fotomuseum' watermark — failing the task's explicit 'not watermarked' image requirement. The collection site collectie.nederlandsfotomuseum.nl runs Axiell Internet Server (AIS6) with the classic Adlib Web API (/webapi/wwwopac.ashx?database=museum&output=json), no auth, 755,494 records. In-scope positive photographic prints (object_name='Afdruk') = 42,535 with real named photographers (Werner Mantz, Ed van der Elsken, Eva Besnyo, Chas Gerretsen, John Fernhout, Lucebert). Metadata is rich and reliably parseable from the detail HTML (/Details/museum/{priref}): creator, description/title, date (Opnamedatum), material, technique, dimensions, B&W flag. Full-res images come from the museum's own image server /webapi-images/wwwopac.ashx?command=getcontent and download at 1185x1600 / 1291x1600 (well over 600px). HOWEVER: the watermark is baked into the stored master itself — present at EVERY resolution (full, 300px, thumbnail) AND every format (JPEG and the 6.2MB TIFF master), covering the entire image area as repeating 'Nederlands Fotomuseum' tiles (verified visually on 3 separate works incl. the Capa/Fernhout print and a Cas Oorthuys contact sheet). No clean path on museum infra: IIIF endpoints 302 to error, /Details/download is blocked (302 to login/error), and the reproduction.identifier_URL / PID_data.URI fields are empty. A watermark this heavy is unusable for a SigLIP visual-discovery grid (it dominates the image and poisons embeddings). Un-watermarked copies exist only on Europeana/Wikimedia, which are FORBIDDEN aggregators. Therefore not viable as a flat-photograph source despite the strong API.
easy_source_found: Yes (metadata/API), but image-blocked. The museum's own Adlib Web API is a de-facto open JSON source: GET https://collectie.nederlandsfotomuseum.nl/webapi/wwwopac.ashx?database=museum&search=<adlib>&output=json&fields=...&startfrom=N&limit=K — no key, returns nested Adlib records (priref, object_number, creator, title, dating.date.start/end, material, technique, dimension.*, Media reference). Detail HTML at /Details/museum/{priref} is the most complete per-record view. No /opendata, /api/v1, IIIF, GitHub dump, or Solr. The blocker is purely the watermark burned into the only image-delivery endpoint (wwwopac.ashx getcontent), not source availability.
probe_summary: Pipeline itself WORKS end-to-end (15/15 built, R2 verified at 1291x1600 webp), but the produced images are full-frame watermarked, so the probe is a FAIL on the 'not watermarked' acceptance criterion. node scripts/scrape-nederlands-fotomuseum.mjs --probe enumerated 50 Afdruk records -> 23 candidates with web image+creator -> enriched via detail HTML -> built 15 finished works (min4-drops 5, 3 rejected as <600px) with title 15/15, artist 15/15, year 15/15, medium 14/15, date 15/15, dimensions 3/15. Real works confirmed (Werner Mantz 1956, Ed van der Elsken Hong Kong 1959, John Fernhout 'Robert Capa as bullfighter' ~1940, Chas Gerretsen 'Apocalypse Now' 1976, Eva Besnyo 1937). One R2 webp verified live (1291x1600, 149KB) — and on visual inspection it carries the tiled 'Nederlands Fotomuseum' watermark across the whole frame, same as the source JPEG and the 6.2MB TIFF master. Probe collection JSON was deleted (would have pointed at watermarked images); the 15 watermarked R2 webps are left as harmless orphans. Server is also notably flaky (frequent 503/504/empty-reply under any load; limit=0 count queries 504), which the script handles with small pages + exponential backoff, but that is secondary to the watermark blocker.

exhibitions_entry.name: Nederlands Fotomuseum
exhibitions_entry.description: The Netherlands' national museum of photography, in Rotterdam's Las Palmas building on the Wilhelminapier. It holds the country's photographic heritage — over 5 million negatives and prints, including the archives of major Dutch photographers such as Cas Oorthuys, Ed van der Elsken and Eva Besnyo — alongside changing exhibitions.
exhibitions_entry.description_ko: 로테르담 빌헬미나피르의 라스팔마스 건물에 자리한 네덜란드 국립 사진미술관이다. 카스 오르타위스, 에드 판 데르 엘스컨, 에바 베스뇨 등 주요 네덜란드 사진가들의 아카이브를 비롯해 500만 점이 넘는 네거티브와 프린트로 네덜란드 사진 유산을 보존하며, 기획전을 함께 연다.

notes: NOT REGISTERED (viable:false). DECISION = watermark blocker: the deliverable image requirement (clean >=600px) cannot be met from museum-own infra; clean copies only on forbidden aggregators. The scrape-nederlands-fotomuseum.mjs script is a COMPLETE, working Adlib pipeline (enumerate Afdruk via API brief -> enrich via detail HTML -> getcontent full-res image -> sharp webp -> R2; resumable --full with <23MB cap, prioritizing named+dated) and would flip to viable immediately if the museum ever (a) exposes an un-watermarked endpoint, (b) publishes an open-data dump, or (c) grants API/image access. SCOPE NOTE for any future attempt: the DB is ~81% Negatief (negatives, out of scope), ~7.5% Diapositief (slides), ~10% Contactafdruk (multi-frame contact sheets, visually weak); only object_name='Afdruk' (42,535) is the clean positive-print set. Photographs are correctly NOT colour-gated (B&W 'zwart-wit' prints kept). Field names (Adlib English tags): creator, dating.date.start/end, material, technique, dimension.value/unit/type, object_name, object_category; media via Media[].media.reference.reference_number + media.original_file_name. CAVEAT: a wide fields= projection truncates in grouped responses, so metadata must come from the detail HTML, not a big fields= list. Image URL pattern (watermarked): /webapi-images/wwwopac.ashx?command=getcontent&server=main&data={reference_number}&value={original_file_name}&imageformat=jpg (omit width/height for native size; &imageformat=tif gives a TIFF master, also watermarked).
